arch_per_gcpsg009hvm: GOVERNMENT GUIDE: RCMP, GCPSG-009 (2022) Security Fencing Considerations Guide, effective 2022-01-27, approved 2022-03-16, page modified 2025-11-03 (official RCMP page; supplements register rcmpGCPSG009 and arch_sec2_gcpsg009b): 8.2 ASTM F2656 'details the requirements for the Hostile Vehicle Mitigation measures'; M30 (K4) 30 mph, M40 (K8) 40 mph, M50 (K12) 50 mph, 15,000 lb vehicle; P1 <1 m, P2 1.1-7 m, P3 7-30 m, P4 ≥30.1 m penetration; 'there is no limit to how far the vehicle can travel past the barrier to be certified'; protection depends on 'the setback and standoff distances' set by a TRA. 9.1 bollards, large planters or rocks as 'larger, more robust vehicular security barriers' where pedestrian traffic is high; back-filled retaining wall as a vehicle barrier; 'Blast pressure falls off with increased standoff'. 9.1, 9.5 ditches and berms. 10.3.2, 10.5 fences with 'integral crash beams or cables'. 10.6 gate barriers: fixed or movable bollards, wedge/ramp barriers, locking arms, cable barriers; 'the first choice to protect a gate is to limit the approach speed of a vehicle' (curves, chicanes, parallel approach); halving speed cuts impact force to a quarter; gates latch 'approximately every four feet of vertical height'. 10.1 minimum security fence 2.4 m, high security ≥3.6 m. 5 and 9.4: provincial or municipal laws and AHJ height limits may restrict fences. No bollard spacing. — https://rcmp.ca/en/lead-security-agency-physical-security/guidance-and-publications/gcpsg-009-2022-security-fencing-considerations-guide
